3. A valid noncommutative all-order operation

The earlier failure of a scalar logarithmic polymer formula remains. There is, however, a different exact operation.

Suppose an operator hard-core gas has the form
$F(s)=
\sum_{\Gamma\ \mathrm{compatible}}
\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma}A_\gamma(s),
\tag{10}$
where compatible activities have disjoint footprints and therefore commute.

A heap is an ordered word modulo exchanges of compatible letters. For a heap with a unique minimal occurrence, differentiate that occurrence and leave the remaining ordered factors unchanged; denote the resulting word by $A'_{\mathrm{root}}(h)$.

Then
$\boxed{
F'F^{-1}
=
\sum_{h:\,\mathrm{unique\ minimal\ occurrence}}
(-1)^{|h|-1}A'_{\mathrm{root}}(h).
}
\tag{11}$
This follows from the valid Cartier–Foata inverse identity in a partially commuting algebra. In $F'F^{-1}$, every additional minimal occurrence can be assigned either to the initial compatible set or to the inverse heap. Its alternating cancellation leaves only the uniquely rooted heaps. No incompatible factors are exchanged. mat.univie.ac.at <https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~slc/books/cartfoa.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com>


Explicit norm hypothesis and conclusion

Let $Y_\gamma$ be connected footprints and
$m_\gamma\ge\max\{1,|Y_\gamma|\}.$
Suppose, uniformly on the parameter interval,
$\|A_\gamma\|\le a_\gamma,
\qquad
\|A'_\gamma\|\le M m_\gamma a_\gamma.$
For $\mu,\nu,\alpha>0$, assume the operator-norm activity condition
$S:=
\sup_i
\sum_{\gamma:\,i\in Y_\gamma}
a_\gamma
e^{\mu\operatorname{diam}(Y_\gamma)+(\nu+\alpha)m_\gamma}
\le\alpha.
\tag{12}$
Then (11) converges absolutely in each finite volume. It supplies an interaction decomposition
$R:=F'F^{-1}=\sum_XR_X$
with
$\boxed{
\sup_i\sum_{X\ni i}
e^{\mu\operatorname{diam}(X)}\|R_X\|
\le \frac{M}{\nu}S.
}
\tag{13}$
The proof uses ordinary scalar Kotecký–Preiss convergence only as a positive counting majorant after establishing the correct operator identity. Set
$w_\gamma
=
a_\gamma e^{\mu\operatorname{diam}(Y_\gamma)+\nu m_\gamma},
\qquad
c_\gamma=\alpha m_\gamma.$
The overlap condition gives
$\sum_{\delta\not\sim\gamma}w_\delta e^{c_\delta}
\le |Y_\gamma|S
\le c_\gamma.$
The differentiated root contributes at most $M\sum m_\gamma$; the spare mass factor pays for it using $x\le e^{\nu x}/\nu$. A marked occurrence anchors the cluster at the specified site. This proves (13).
